note: Aruba, read 2026-10-31. Majority: the Civil Code of Aruba (Burgerlijk Wetboek van Aruba, 2nd edition, September 2024, published by the Government on its site), Book 1, art. 233: minors are those who haven't reached eighteen and aren't and haven't been married or declared of age under art. 253ha; so majority is 18, marriage and the court's declaration of age not held. Art. 234: a minor acting with the consent of his legal representative may perform legal acts, and consent is presumed for acts usual for minors of his age (not held). Work: the Arbeidsverordening 2013 (AB 2013 no. 14, of 12 March 2013, issued 21 March 2013; the Government's legislative department's copy on archive.org), art. 1 calls children those under fifteen and young persons those of fifteen to seventeen, and art. 19(1) bars letting children work, paid or not; so 15. Performers: art. 19(3) lets the Director (of the labour department), on written request and with conditions, grant an exemption (ontheffing) for work by children of thirteen or older that is needed to learn a trade, is by its nature done by children, or isn't physically or mentally demanding or dangerous, outside school hours and between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.; a young performer's work is held to fall under it (my reading), so performers need the Director's exemption, from 13, and none is given younger. The young persons' limits (art. 20, night and dangerous work) aren't held. Service: the Netherlands Antilles' Dienstplichtverordening 1961 (P.B. 1961, no. 223) is still on the books (Curaçao republished its implementing decree of 1964 in consolidated form on 3 December 2025, P.B. 2025 no. 171) and Aruba amended its own Dienstplichtverordening in 1986 (AB 1986 no. 40, found by its title, not read); but whether anyone is called under it now, and from what age, wasn't found: Defence's page on the Caribbean (defensie.nl) names the Arumil and Curmil and the Social Formation Track (SVT) without saying how they are filled, and the Curaçao Chronicle (July 2026) reports a petition against a possible Kingdom-wide conscription, describing only the Netherlands' suspended draft. So service is null.
